clue.text: With opener dismissed, more than one drawing lots

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, and dismissing it sends it away from the front of the word

parts.note: idle sketches are doodles, plural here

explanation.surface: A cricket side has lost its opening batsman while lots are being drawn for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener dismissed' sounds like cricket, but it just removes the D at the front of DOODLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a great quantity of something is described as heaps or plenty.

parts.note: zero, written as the round letter O
a forbidding manner is stern and gloomy, i.e. dour

explanation.surface: Someone's good name stays clean because nothing was banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, as in 'in bad odour', meaning in poor repute.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be in good or bad odour with people is to have that standing or esteem with them.

definitions.meaning: unconventional or out of the mainstream
a player sent off has departed the pitch, so has quit the playing area

explanation.surface: A firebrand player has been shown the red card.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means unorthodox; read literally, the two words say someone departed the playing area.

indicators.note: one word keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or error
a hut is a small shed

explanation.surface: A mistake meant the garden shed got enclosed by a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something enclosed or confined so it cannot get out has been closed in.

indicators.note: to jog something is to jolt or shake it, so the letters of the next words are shaken up

explanation.surface: A runner jogs past and circles round the edge of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' looks like the runner's action but is the anagram signal on BY AROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an edge or limit marking where an area ends.

clue.text: Fraud in equestrian competition? One's taken to court

parts.note: Badminton Horse Trials is a famous English three-day eventing competition
a racket is a dishonest scheme or swindle

explanation.surface: A swindle has been uncovered at a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton is an English country estate that hosts major horse trials; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic hint: the item a player carries onto a badminton court for a game.

indicators.note: letters that misbehave do not stay in their places, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebellious child gets grounded for acting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounded' looks like a punishment but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the contender thought least likely to win, as in a long-shot competitor.

indicators.note: one piece placed before another comes first in the answer

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits, swallowed as a drink

explanation.surface: A theatregoer downs a whisky before the curtain rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stage work for actors is a theatrical piece.

clue.text: Stuffed by nobleman, Conservative gets a shiner

indicators.note: the outer word is stuffed by the inner, which fills it

parts.note: conservatives are the political right
an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is beaten up by an aristocrat and ends with a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a shiner' suggests a black eye, but here it is just a thing that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic sense: a lamp at the back of a vehicle or bicycle literally gives off light.

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
to set up a business is to found it

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a scam that has been rigged against them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old-fashioned expletive adjective meaning damned or blasted.

clue.text: A whip cut, I'm sorry to say

indicators.note: a word that is cut loses its tail

parts.note: a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: An apologetic admission that a whip has been trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Interjection: an expression of regret, as in unfortunately.

clue.text: Airmen prepared to be caught by US soldier, writing on the wall

indicators.note: pieces caught by another are held inside it

parts.note: GI is the usual term for an American soldier
the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force
fit means ready or prepared, as in fit for action

explanation.surface: British airmen are arrested by an American soldier for daubing a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal description: words or pictures scrawled or sprayed on walls in public.

definitions.meaning: an intensifier, as in so good or truly good
a sceptical one-word retort, as in 'Is that so?'

explanation.surface: A doubting reply in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means very or truly, and on its own as a question it voices disbelief.

clue.text: Long bag snipped at both ends

indicators.note: a word snipped at both ends loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a sachet is a small sealed bag

explanation.surface: A long bag has been cut open top and bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the bag, but it is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym verb: to pine or yearn for something you lack.

clue.text: Attempt to suppress principal in Cambridge, light blue

indicators.note: the principal letter of a word is its first

parts.note: a lamp gives light
feeling blue is feeling low or down

explanation.surface: A college head at Cambridge wears the university's light blue colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge's sporting colour is light blue, but here 'light' and 'blue' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym noun: a crackdown, an official effort to stamp out an activity.

indicators.note: one piece maintaining another keeps it held inside

parts.note: when you are through, you are finished or done

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A school that keeps discipline from the start is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school, but here it is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: complete and detailed, leaving nothing out.

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A radio station played a tune in its proper running slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: arranged neatly and systematically, tidy and structured.

clue.text: From pass and save, some goal?

parts.note: in football a cross is a pass into the centre from the wing
save and bar both mean except

explanation.surface: A football commentator describes part of a goal from a pass and a save.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like a goalkeeper's stop but means except, i.e. bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the horizontal beam along the top of the posts is one part of a goal.

definitions.meaning: a small citrus fruit like a tangerine
a language, here the standard Chinese one

explanation.surface: Two bare nouns: a fruit and a language.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small loose-skinned citrus fruit and the main spoken language of China.

parts.note: got can mean became, as in got angry
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A kind of rock has hardened over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests geology, but it is a style of rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dark, gloomy genre of post-punk music with its own subculture.

indicators.note: the letters are held within the run of the following words

explanation.surface: A political view firmly maintained by Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an attitude or standpoint, or a way of standing.

clue.text: Little boy after somewhere for bathing suit

indicators.note: the first named piece comes after the second

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral baths
Des is the short form of the boy's name Desmond

explanation.surface: A young lad chasing after a bathing suit at a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bathing suit' runs together in the surface, but 'suit' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the four card suits in a standard pack.

indicators.note: the outer word covers the inner, wrapping round it

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: A gathering spreads over a fresh versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Florentine writer of the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Great weight is in wood — stagger

indicators.note: pieces put in another sit inside it

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: A heavy load in a forest makes someone stagger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stagger' looks like a stumbling walk but means to amaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to amaze or stun someone greatly.

clue.text: Old transporter in which Irishman carries daughter

indicators.note: the outer word carries the inner inside it

parts.note: Sean is a typically Irish first name
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An old conveyance in which an Irish father carries his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical example: an enclosed chair carried on poles by bearers.

definitions.meaning: a do held indoors, i.e. a party at home
to kill someone, a slang phrasal verb

explanation.surface: A shriek at a party where someone has been killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is an indoor party; as slang phrasal verb it means kill.

clue.text: Muddle bad, go in and ask for cleaner

indicators.note: to muddle letters is to jumble them out of order

explanation.surface: A confused instruction to go in and fetch a cleaning product.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: sodium bicarbonate is widely used as a household cleaning agent.

indicators.note: letters repaired are reassembled into a new order

explanation.surface: A building at the heart of town has been fixed without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym phrase: done confidentially, without others knowing.

indicators.note: the capital letter, the first one, is used up and gone

parts.note: a bank lending money is offering loans

explanation.surface: A bank stops offering loans once its funds run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym noun: the conclusion or close of something.
